cases.expected: NumericIndicator whose getValue(0) returns 95 (original delegate value 100 minus 5)
cases.description: Verify that minus(Number) correctly creates a constant indicator from a positive Integer and subtracts it from the delegate.

cases.expected: NumericIndicator whose getValue(0) returns 24.7 (original delegate value 20.5 minus -4.2)
cases.description: Check that a negative Double is handled as a constant and subtraction works (adds the absolute value).

cases.expected: NumericIndicator whose getValue(0) returns 0 (original delegate value 0 minus 0)
cases.description: Edge case where the constant is zero; the result should be identical to the original delegate.
Passing a null Number should cause a NullPointerException when createConstant(n) is invoked.

cases.expected: NumericIndicator whose getValue(0) returns 900000000 (original delegate value 1000000000 minus 100000000)
cases.description: Validate handling of large numeric values (BigDecimal representation) without overflow.

group: minus(Number) with different numeric types (Long, Float)

cases.expected: NumericIndicator whose getValue(0) returns -1234567890023 (original delegate value -10 minus 1234567890123)
cases.description: Ensure that Long values are correctly converted to a constant indicator and subtracted.

cases.expected: NumericIndicator whose getValue(0) returns 6.86 (original delegate value 10.0 minus 3.14)
cases.description: Confirm that Float/Double values are handled with proper precision.

cases.expected: NumericIndicator whose getValue(0) returns 8 (original delegate value 15 minus 7) and getValue(1) returns 13 (original delegate value 20 minus 7)
cases.description: Validate that a Short (auto‑boxed from int literal) is correctly turned into a constant indicator and subtracted from a delegate that has different values at multiple indices.

cases.expected: NumericIndicator whose getValue(0) returns -3 (original delegate value -5 minus -2)
cases.description: Check handling of a negative Byte constant; the subtraction should effectively add the absolute value.

cases.expected: NumericIndicator whose getValue(0) returns -12345678901234567890 (original delegate value 0 minus the BigInteger constant)
cases.description: Ensure that a BigInteger (passed as a Number via its toString representation) is accepted, converted to a Num, and subtracted without overflow.
When the constant is Double.NaN the resulting Num should also be NaN, propagating the undefined value.

cases.expected: NumericIndicator whose getValue(0) is -Infinity (original delegate value finite minus +Infinity)
cases.description: Test subtraction of a positive infinite constant; the result must be negative infinite according to IEEE‑754 rules.

cases.expected: NumericIndicator whose getValue(0) returns 20 (original delegate value 30 minus 10)
cases.description: Verify that any subclass of java.lang.Number (e.g., java.util.concurrent.atomic.AtomicInteger) is correctly handled by createConstant.

cases.expected: NumericIndicator (result of minus(5).plus(3)) whose getValue(0) returns 48 (original delegate value 50 minus 5 plus 3)
cases.description: Confirm that minus(Number) returns a NumericIndicator that can be further chained; the intermediate result should be correct.

cases.expected: NumericIndicator whose getValue(2) equals SMA(closePrice, 3) at index 2 minus 2.5
cases.description: Apply minus(Number) to a non‑constant delegate (SMA of close prices). Verify subtraction works for a non‑trivial index (e.g., 2) where SMA has already performed averaging.

group: minus(Number) with Number subclass that throws RuntimeException in doubleValue

cases.description: A custom Number implementation whose doubleValue() method throws a RuntimeException should cause minus(Number) to propagate that exception when createConstant(n) attempts to read the numeric value.

group: minus(Number) with excessively large BigDecimal causing overflow

cases.description: When a BigDecimal with a magnitude far beyond the range supported by the underlying Num implementation is supplied, the conversion inside createConstant should fail and throw an ArithmeticException (or a similar overflow‑related exception).
